title: L2 weak elliptic regularity for bundle operators
statement: All vector spaces are over the real field $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $N$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $m\geq1$, with a smooth Riemannian metric and volume form. Let $G,H$ be smooth real vector bundles of the same finite rank, with smooth positive definite fibre metrics. Let $Q:\Gamma^\infty(G)\to\Gamma^\infty(H)$ be a real-linear differential operator with smooth coefficients of order at most $k\geq1$, locally $Q=\sum_{|\alpha|\leq k}b_\alpha(x)\partial^\alpha$, whose degree-$k$ principal symbol $\sum_{|\alpha|=k}b_\alpha(x)\xi^\alpha:G_x\to H_x$ is invertible for every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi$. Let $u$ be an $L^2$ section of $G$ (a measurable section modulo almost-everywhere equality with $\int_N|u|^2\,dV<\infty$). Regard $u$ as a distributional section, and define $Qu$ in each smooth frame by the displayed differential expression using distributional derivatives. If $Qu$ is the distribution induced by a smooth section of $H$, then $u$ is the distribution induced by a smooth section of $G$; equivalently $u$ has a smooth representative.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, Gårding inequality (2.3) and Sobolev lemma (2.1), printed p.289; smooth-right-hand-side consequence for bundle-valued systems; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-differential-formal-adjoint-symbol] to $Q$ with $d=k$, obtaining $Q^*:H\to G$. On the metric bundle $B=G\oplus H$ define $P(a,b)=(Q^*b,Qa)$. This is an order-at-most-$k$ smooth differential endomorphism. If $A=\sigma_k(Q)(x,\xi)$ for $\xi\neq0$, its symbol sends $(a,b)$ to $((-1)^k A^*b,Aa)$, with inverse $(c,e)\mapsto(A^{-1}e,(-1)^k(A^*)^{-1}c)$. Thus $P$ has invertible degree-$k$ symbol on a single bundle. Set $w=(u,0)$ and write $f$ for the given smooth representative of $Qu$. Distributional differentiation is componentwise, so $Pw=(0,f)$.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §1 (1.5)--(1.7); agent block-matrix reduction of the two-bundle operator to a one-bundle operator; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: For each integer $s\geq0$, $Pw=(0,f)$ belongs to $H^s(B)$. To check this using the norms in the cited estimate, take a finite coordinate trivializing cover and apply [lem-sfb-smooth-subordinate-partition] with closed set $S=N$. Compactness makes $N$ sigma-compact and each closed subordinate support compact inside its chart. Every derivative of the smooth localized section is bounded on that compact support, hence square integrable. Now apply [lem-sfb-weak-garding-sobolev-estimate] with $v=w$, $d=k$ and this $s$. The base is compact without boundary, $B$ has its direct-sum positive definite metric, $w$ is $L^2$, and the symbol was checked in step 1. The weak version of the estimate gives $w\in H^{s+k}(B)$ for every $s\geq0$ without assuming any derivatives of $w$ beforehand.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2 (2.3); smooth right-hand side has finite localized Sobolev norms; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Fix an integer $r\geq0$. Choose an integer $s\geq0$ so large that $s+k>r+m/2$. Step 2 gives $w\in H^{s+k}(B)$, so [lem-sfb-bundle-sobolev-embedding], with $t=s+k$, yields a $C^r$ representative $w_r$ of this same $L^2$ class. This also supplies a continuous representative $w_0$ by taking $r=0$. The strict inequality, the dimension and the compact metric-bundle hypotheses are precisely those in the cited embedding.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2 (2.1) applied at arbitrarily large finite Sobolev order; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf

proof.text: Each $w_r$ is continuous and represents the same $L^2$ class $w$. By the uniqueness of the continuous representative in [lem-sfb-bundle-sobolev-embedding] applied to the $r=0$ instance in step 3, $w_r=w_0$ pointwise. Hence the single section $w_0$ is $C^r$ for every nonnegative integer $r$, which is the definition of smoothness in local coordinates. Its projection onto $G$ is smooth and equals $u$ almost everywhere. This is the requested smooth representative.

source.place: WANTED locally; Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, VI §2, assembly of (2.3) and (2.1); agent argument identifying the representatives at different finite orders; read online https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf
